Consult Summary:
42-year-old woman with 2-hour history of continuous spinning vertigo, ear buzzing, and nausea; clinician impression is labyrinthitis with prescription for symptomatic relief and in-person follow-up arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden-onset dizziness described as “room is spinning,” accompanied by nausea and buzzing in both ears.  
• Onset & course: Began ≈2 hours prior while making breakfast; has persisted without relief. Prior similar but brief (5–10 min) episode 1 month ago that resolved spontaneously.  
• Aggravating/relieving factors: None identified; not clearly positional.  
• Associated symptoms: Unsteady gait (feels she cannot walk straight), shakiness, tinnitus. No vomiting yet, no headache, no limb weakness, no visual changes, no hearing loss, no ear pain or discharge, no recent viral illness, no fever.  
• Pertinent negatives: No focal neurologic deficits reported.

Past Medical History:
• Premature ovarian failure; on hormone-replacement therapy (HRT).  
• No other chronic medical or surgical conditions reported.

Medications:
• HRT – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• New prescription sent today (medication name not captured on audio) – 1 tablet PO three times daily for 10 days.  
Allergies: Denies drug or other allergies.

Social History:
• Married; preparing breakfast for husband at symptom onset.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use: not discussed (missing).

Family History:
• Not discussed (missing).

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (video consultation).  
• General/Neurologic: Patient reports intact strength; feels unsteady but able to ambulate. No formal exam performed or documented.  
• Otologic: No direct visualization; patient denies otalgia or discharge.  
(Overall: Physical examination not recorded.)

Investigations:
• None performed during video visit.  
• Plan to obtain blood pressure and otoscopic examination at in-person appointment.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Acute vestibular syndrome most consistent with labyrinthitis/vestibular neuritis.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Vestibular neuritis / labyrinthitis – continuous vertigo, tinnitus, nausea, no focal deficits (supports). Lack of preceding viral illness or hearing loss (against but does not rule out).  
2. Ménière’s disease – recurrent vertigo and tinnitus (supports); no fluctuating hearing loss (against).  
3. Posterior-circulation stroke/TIA – acute vertigo with gait unsteadiness (supports); age 42, no risk factors, no neurologic signs (against).

Issue 1: Acute vertigo with suspected labyrinthitis  
• Start symptomatic medication (name inaudible) 1 tablet PO TID ×10 days.  
• Arrange in-person review with primary-care doctor for otoscopic exam, blood pressure, and gait/neuro assessment.  
• Advise patient to avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until symptoms resolve.  

Issue 2: Nausea associated with vertigo  
• Symptomatic medication above expected to alleviate dizziness and nausea.  
• Encourage adequate oral hydration and small, light meals as tolerated.  

Issue 3: Safety-netting / red-flag monitoring  
• Educated patient to attend Emergency Department if she develops limb weakness, sudden severe headache, violent vomiting, or any worsening neurological symptoms before scheduled review.  
• Provided instructions to contact clinic support to book follow-up appointment.

General Plan Items:  
• Pharmacy: Prescription sent electronically to Lloyds Pharmacy.  
• Follow-up: In-person appointment within next few days; sooner if deterioration.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: Detailed vital signs, full neurologic and otologic examination, social habits, family history.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Medication name inaudible; otherwise clear.
